title: Move or rename a file or directory
summary: Use the mv command to move files to a new location or rename them. If the target is a directory, the file is moved inside it; otherwise, it is renamed.

steps.explain: Move a file or directory to a new path. If the target path does not exist as a directory, the source is renamed to the target name.

placeholders.name: SOURCE
placeholders.description: Path to the file or directory you want to move or rename

placeholders.name: TARGET
placeholders.description: New name or path for the file/directory

steps.explain: Move a file or directory into an existing directory. The filename remains unchanged.

placeholders.name: SOURCE
placeholders.description: Path to the file or directory you want to move

steps.explain: Move multiple files into an existing directory at once.

rollback.explain: Move the file back to its original location using the reverse mv command.

placeholders.name: TARGET
placeholders.description: Current path of the moved file

warnings: Moving a file overwrites the target if it already exists, unless you use flags like --interactive or --no-clobber.
